newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Ex-Burnfield duo join UMECO.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Ex-Burnfield duo join UMECO.

text.p: Two ex-heads of Burnfield Plc joined the board of UMECO Plc on Wednesday and paid 2.0 million stg for a "significant" stake in a company with strong growth prospects, one of them told Reuters in a telephone interview.

"Part of the attraction of UMECO was its relative smallness in that Brian (McGowan) and I wanted to have a significant stake in the new venture, but if the company is too large you end up with a ....relatively low stake." said Clive Snowdon. "It fitted our bill extremely well".

The stake gives McGowan and Snowdon over five percent of UMECO's share capital. McGowan is chairman of department store chain House of Fraser Plc and was Burnfield chairman until January. Snowdon was managing director of Burnfield.

"We are both making a serious personal investment, and clearly looking to get value from that investment over the medium term. We're not short-term operators," said Snowdon, citing his five years and McGowan's seven years at Burnfield.
Systems manufacturer Burnfield was acquired by electronics and engineering manufacturer Fairey Plc in January.

UMECO has been trading very successfully. In a statement the group estimated pre-tax profit for the year to end-March of not less than 2.5 million stg and a total dividend of 5.5 pence per share, up 29 percent.
"We didn't want to go into a moribund group. Finding a small company which is growing at that rate is difficult. There's not many of them around," said Snowdon.

UMECO said it has arranged a placing and open offer of 4.09 million new shares at 240 pence each to meet the costs of a 9.2 million stg acquisition. McGowan and Snowdon had agreed to take up an aggregate 2.0 million stg in the placing.
"By taking up a large chunk of the placing we're going to end up with over five percent of the enlarged group share capital and for us that is an important benchmark number," said Snowdon.

Snowdon and McGowan become chief executive and chairman respectively of UMECO on April 28. The current chairman, George Metcalfe, remains as a non-executive director but retires from the board at the Annual General Meeting in July.
Snowdon and McGowan see UMECO -- a distributor of aerospace components and resins, and manufacturer of aircraft refuelling equipment and metal tubing -- having excellent growth prospects.

"We're very much looking forward to starting on Monday and taking the group forward. I think it's got excellent prospects and I believe with the energy we can put into it you will see the already successful rate of growth moving even more sharply in the future".

Metcalfe had welcomed the new appointments of McGowan and Snowdon. "Both bring considerable relevant experience to the group and a strong commitment to its future development, a commitment supported by the material financial investment they are making in UMECO," he added in a statement.

UMECO said it is acquiring Wellmar, parent company of G.R.P. Materials Supplies Ltd -- independent distributor of polyester resin, glass fibre and complementary products to manufacturers of plastic products.

UMECO will make further acquisitions in the next few months if it can find some as good as G.R.P. which Snowdon called "an excellent fit and a very good price and it substantially enhances their earnings for the short-term and medium term".
